AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in. On 6 October, OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, released more than 700 preprints written by AI, claiming to have solved more than 300 major open problems in mathematics. Some researchers stayed up all night combing through the papers that the company had posted, anxious to know whether their entire research programmes had been rendered obsolete overnight.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Depending on who you ask, this was either the most progress or the most catastrophic development ever to happen in one day in the history of the field — or both. Either way, mathematicians realized that their profession would never be the same. “It’s probably the end of mathematics as we know it,” theoretical physicist Miranda Cheng mentioned at an emergency meeting on mathematics and AI at the Royal Society in London in late October. Many of the papers cracked problems by combining ideas from disparate parts of the discipline, leveraging a universality of knowledge that no human could ever match — and leaving even some of the world’s smartest people feeling completely outdone.

Since then, one of the field’s greatest outstanding challenges, the Riemann hypothesis, also appears to have been solved with AI assistance. And mathematicians across the world have joined frantic collective efforts to confront challenges raised by AI’s advances, from how to evaluate and publish research papers to how to raise future generations of mathematicians. Some see the risk as existential. If mathematical problem-solving becomes mainly a machine endeavour — seen as a utility like water or electricity — then their profession could lose its status in society and human expertise might start to dwindle.

“It’s a challenge like we’ve never faced in mathematics — or in academia as a whole,” states Simon Machado, a mathematician at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) in Zurich.

In a recent development, the bombshell paper drop in October came on the heels of earlier shocks to the field. OpenAI, which is based in San Francisco, California, released a batch of ten notable results in August and, in early September, followed up with a historic solution to the Navier–Stokes problem about how fluids flow. The firm had been making noises to indicate that much more was to come. Still, many researchers were surprised by the enormity of the 6 October release. “To just see it as a giant list, without the care and thought and the love that goes into doing this work on a normal basis, it was really jarring,” says Catherine Cossaboom, a master’s student in mathematics at the University of Oxford, UK.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps no source has documented the moment better than Proofs and Prompts, an online forum that publishes essays on the impact of AI on mathematics. An 8 October post titled “100+ reactions to 100+ solutions” collected immediate reactions from dozens of students and career researchers to OpenAI’s 6 October drop. Some wrote poems, others quoted the writers Leo Tolstoy and Stanisław Lem, still others posted fragments from the Gospels (in the original Greek). One contribution reinterpreted the lyrics of ‘Jolene’ by the late country singer Dolly Parton:.

And I can easily understand / How you could easily take my math / But you don’t know what it means to me, AI.

The tone ranged from the enthusiastic to the angry and the despondent. “Some of them made me really feel heartbroken,” claims Albane Théry, an applied mathematician at the University of Warwick in Coventry, UK, who is one of the volunteer moderators of the forum.

Few subfields of mathematics were spared and some were thoroughly ravaged. “Not a single one of the major open problems I have publicly mentioned throughout my career was left untouched,” Fields Medal winner Hugo Duminil-Copin wrote to Proofs and Prompts. “I expected that one day we would be surpassed, and that it would happen systematically. But yesterday’s announcement hit with a force I had not anticipated.”.

Hugo Duminil-Copin fears that AI will eclipse human understanding of mathematics.Credit: Chris Peus.

Recent findings suggest that duminil-Copin, who is at the University of Geneva in Switzerland, specializes in the theory of transitions in complex systems — such as those that determine how information or infection filters through social networks or how metals can acquire magnetization. (OpenAI’s rival Anthropic, also in San Francisco, had already claimed to have solved a major result in this field in late August.).

Industry observers note that another field that bore a massive impact was the theory of groups — some of the most ubiquitous structures across mathematics, physics and other disciplines. For example, the possible ways of shuffling a deck of cards — and what happens when you revert a shuffle or combine several together — constitute a group, as do the infinite possible ways of rotating a solid object in 3D.

Recent findings suggest that openAI’s August batch already contained the solution to a key problem on groups. Soon after its release, during a YouTube interview, Francesco Fournier-Facio, a group theorist at Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh, UK, mentioned two other problems that mathematicians could now attack with the help of AI. Within days, he was emailed by a PhD student in computational biology who had used OpenAI’s large language model (LLM) GPT 5.6 Sol to solve one of those problems.

According to recent reports, can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

According to recent reports, can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

Fournier-Facio says that OpenAI’s October dump was even more impactful for him personally. It included the solution to a problem on which he had been actively working, called the Boone–Higman conjecture. Overall, OpenAI released solutions to perhaps eight of the top ten problems that Fournier-Facio had dreamed of solving during his career, he told Nature.

In a recent development, but the most stunning AI result relates to what many researchers see as the most key open problem in all of mathematics. The Riemann hypothesis, a question that was posed in the mid-nineteenth century by the German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, centres on whether prime numbers are scattered across the set of all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as unpredictable as it could be.

AI assistance seems to have cracked it. First, OpenAI proved a partial result, called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, in its October dump. Then, on 20 November, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge revealed that he had found a proof of the full Riemann hypothesis, working with Claude, the firm’s AI assistant. However, that was rapidly followed by a non-AI assisted proof by Rome-based mathematician Alessandro Masullo, which he had been working on for years. “If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” indicates number theorist James Maynard, a Fields Medal winner at the University of Oxford.

Maynard and many other researchers are excited by AI technology. It is “quite likely to unleash a golden age of mathematical discovery”, he said at the meeting. Another mathematician, Antoine Tilloy at the Mines Paris engineering school, part of PSL University, uses the metaphor that doing mathematics with AI is like riding a dragon: the researcher is still in charge, but the dragon gives them supernatural powers.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

But the speed at which AI proofs are emerging has already produced an immediate negative reaction. For one, mathematicians, who have long prided themselves on their field’s culture of openness, are now wary of discussing their work in public. “People are even scared to put out an abstract for a talk they are about to give on ongoing work,” says Jakub Dobrowolski, a PhD candidate at Queen Mary University of London. “Nobody wants to share newly introduced ideas because of the speed at which somebody else can take them and write a paper,” says Peter Sarnak, a number theorist at Princeton University in New Jersey.

And although established researchers say that they are both thrilled and anxious about reinventing their discipline with AI, younger generations are much more fearful. As Maynard and other established mathematicians acknowledge, the technology already poses severe problems in relation to how to assess merit when peer-reviewing mathematics work that might have been done mostly with AI, and how to train and educate the next generation of mathematicians.

“How do we train people if a good PhD thesis can be prompted out of an LLM? The response from people who are in permanent positions tends to be ‘We’re going to see and discuss’,” says Théry. “But the timescale for that could be too long for postdoc or PhD candidates who will be out of a job in nine months.”.

Sources indicate that many early-career researchers told Nature that this uncertainty is their main source of anxiety right now. “While it is clear that faculty are working hard to find long-term solutions to the problems we are all facing, there doesn’t seem to be as much guidance on what to do in the meantime,” indicates Jad Hamdan, a postdoc mathematician at the University of Oxford. AI poses “more danger the younger you are, and the less experienced you are”, adds Dobrowolski. The toughest problem could be working out how to write a proposal for a research programme that might span two or three years, or more, Dobrowolski says. “Is it realistic? Now I feel like whatever I propose might just expire within a year.”.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

A UK survey of graduate students and academic mathematicians last month by the Martingale Foundation in London found that PhD students in particular are much less optimistic about AI’s impact than are established researchers. Asked if AI would “weaken their development as mathematicians”, 89% of students agreed, compared with only 68% of academics.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have finalised their transfer strategy heading into the winter window.

The Red Devils are languishing in 19th place in the Premier League with just one win all season, in what's becoming their biggest crisis in the modern era.

With upcoming manager Mauricio Pochettino at the wheel, however, plans are already in motion to improve the squad – with new arrivals coming to Old Trafford in January.

Manchester United were battered at the hands of Liverpool at the weekend in Pochettino's bow, which highlighted the problems across the team.

Leny Yoro was sent off early in the fixture, with Matthijs De Ligt criticised on his first Premier League start of the season, as Pochettino's men shipped four at Anfield.

Now, TEAMtalk have reported that United are prioritising a central defender, a left-back and a striker in January.

Calvin Bassey is high on the wish list – with the Fulham man left-footed – with the likes of Jarrad Branthwaite and Nathan Collins also on the radar.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Benjamin Sesko is out until the latest year with injury, with Matheus Cunha starting up front at Liverpool, while Marcus Rashford was an option to sell in the summer but remained at the request of then-manager Michael Carrick.

Ivan Toney and Folarin Balogun are options up front.

Luke Shaw will likely continue as the first-choice left-back with Pochettino having worked with the England man previously at Southampton – though with Shaw now into his 30s and with an unreliable injury record, his days at United could now be numbered.

It is believed, however, that United will not have a lot of money to spend this winter and may have to be clever with players they look to bring in.

Manchester United face Sporting tomorrow night, as Champions League action resumes this week.

Manchester United have transfer war chest to spend on backing Mauricio Pochettino in January

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino has barely unpacked his bags at Old Trafford, but it's already abundantly clear Manchester United need to back their newly introduced head coach in January.
  • Following a disappointing start to the campaign and the arrival of a new regulatory era in English football, the club’s latest financial results offer a clear picture as to how much room INEOS actually have to manoeuvre.
  • Man United’s most recent full-year accounts, covering the 12-month period to 30 June, 2026, which were published in September, paints a picture of cost-cutting paired with historically strong commercial standing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has barely unpacked his bags at Old Trafford, but it's already abundantly clear Manchester United need to back their newly introduced head coach in January.

Following a disappointing start to the campaign and the arrival of a new regulatory era in English football, the club’s latest financial results offer a clear picture as to how much room INEOS actually have to manoeuvre.

Man United’s most recent full-year accounts, covering the 12-month period to 30 June, 2026, which were published in September, paints a picture of cost-cutting paired with historically strong commercial standing.

Despite having no European football last season, Man United posted record revenue of £677.6 million while trimming wages for a third consecutive year to £302.0m.

Although previous recruitment pushed player amortisation to £211.8m and left a net loss of £43.0m after finance costs, £47.0m in player-sale profits kept the underlying business moving forward.

Even more telling are Man United’s first-quarter results for 2026/27, released on November 19.

With Champions League football back at Old Trafford, quarterly revenue rose 4.1 per cent to £146.1m, and the club are predicted to earn £740m and £760m annually.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Quarterly player amortisation fell by almost 15 per cent following summer exits and Casemiro’s contract expiry, while another £20.7m was banked in player-disposal profits.

It has been revealed that this summer, the Premier League replaced Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR) with its new Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) system. Under SCR, clubs’ on-pitch spending - which comprises first-team player and head coach wages, transfer amortisation, and agent fees, while excluding non-playing staff, academy and women’s team costs - is capped at 85 per cent of football revenue plus net profit on player sales.

There is even a 30 per cent multi-year buffer up to a 115 per cent ‘Red Threshold’ before points deductions apply. However, because Man United are competing in the Champions League, they must simultaneously adhere to UEFA’s stricter 70 per cent squad cost limit ahead of the March 1 compliance checkpoint.

Therefore, Pochettino has far more breathing room in the transfer market than naysayers might suggest.

Taking the £750m midpoint of Man United’s expected 2026/27 revenue and adding roughly £45m - which is an average of player-trading profits over recent years - that gives an adjusted revenue figure of £795m.

According to recent reports, under the Premier League’s 85 per cent threshold, Man United could carry £675.8m in annual squad costs. Under UEFA’s tighter 70 per cent ceiling, their limit sits at £556.5m.

Remove non-playing staff from total wages and Man United’s first-team player and coaching bill sits near £255m. Add £186.4m in annualised amortisation and roughly £35m in agents’ fees, and total squad costs land around £476.4m - roughly 60 per cent of adjusted revenue.

That leaves roughly £80m in annual squad-cost headroom beneath UEFA’s 70 per cent cap - and nearly £200m domestically.

This means Man United could comfortably sanction £120m to £150m in winter transfer spending. That said, their borrowing position and existing credit facility could yet prove to be a handbrake on any January rebuild, but from a purely regulatory standpoint, Man United's transfer expenditure picture is a rosy one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:40 EST, 24 November 2026.

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

But United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday.

Sources indicate that ‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’.

In a recent development, united sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ said Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

It has been revealed that ‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’.

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a latest contact stalled.

‘We have time to speak about that,’ stated Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’.

Asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’.

Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw in their Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund but remain on course to qualify in one of the automatic knockout spots.

The Gunners started the clash at the Emirates Stadium in quick fashion and controlled possession with short, slick passes and forward runs. Noni Madueke impressed on the right and set up Viktor Gyokeres to score the opening goal from outside the penalty area.

However, Mikel Arteta’s team slackened off in discipline as the half went on which allowed Dortmund to gain a foothold. The Bundesliga leaders then came out from half-time with renewed vigour and secured an equaliser through Maximilian Beier.

With the scores level both teams created further chances, Declan Rice hit the post and Jobe Bellingham had a goal disallowed, but neither could find the back of the net again.

The points were shared leaving Arsenal fifth in the league phase table with Dortmund one point below them in seventh.

Relive the updates from Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund, below:.

It isn’t yet a real problem for Arsenal, but it may just breathe a bit of life into the number of teams looking up at them: a sudden inability to kill games.

And while that usually refers to finishing - in the sense of scoring - it is here as applicable to their ability to strangle matches.

"That's what we want [to finish in the top eight],” Arteta told Amazon Prime Video.

“We have a significant game against Manchester City at home on Sunday so we need to recover really well, we have four days to do that and sustain that momentum the way we are playing and the win will come.".

The Arsenal manager also spoke about Noni Madueke and his reaction to the result in the dressing room.

Arteta revealed: "He [Madueke] was really good but you go in the dressing room and he is not satisfied because we had so many chances where we can put the ball in the net and finish the action.".

Of his Swedish striker, Mikel Arteta added: "He was great, not only the goal but he connected with the team.

“We found him in various ways in many situations and it was always a threat.".

The Arsenal manager noted: "The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end.

“We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

"I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.”.

"For sure,” Viktor Gyokeres added.

“We are very confident. We will go for it.".

Arsenal’s goalscorer Viktor Gyokeres spoke after the game.

He said: "We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways.

“We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

"The most crucial thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals when games are coming up.".

Manchester City were also held to a draw tonight as they finished their encounter with Napoli 2-2.

Meanwhile, Jude Bellingham scored a screamer in a 5-1 victory for Real Madrid over PSV Eindhoven.

90+4 mins: There’s no late drama.

Arsenal try their best to secure an equaliser but it’s not enough and the points are shared at the Emirates Stadium.

90 mins: Four minutes of added time to play.

Time for some late drama perhaps?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.
  • It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.
  • The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain beat England 1-0 to win the 2023 World Cup.

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.

It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.

The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.

The tournament will consist of 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.

The 'All Together' bid included a proposal to use 19 venues, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

Monday's special meeting of Fifa's Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

The news comes on the same day the UK government revealed a vision for one million more girls to play, watch or be in leadership roles in sport by the time the tournament takes place.

Hosting World Cup means decade of excitement - Weir.

Fifa announces UK will host 2035 Women's World Cup.

England failed to win the right to host the men's World Cups in 2006 and 2018, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for the 2030 tournament was abandoned.

But England and Scotland hosted matches at the men's Euros in 2021, and England staged the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.

England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the men's European Championship in 2028.

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.

"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.".

The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

If Manchester United's proposed fresh Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it would still be considered in its current form.

Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland.

Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government stated in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.

A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's newly introduced Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.

Fifa is yet to decide whether all four co-hosts will qualify automatically.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff is one of two Welsh venues, along with the Cardiff City Stadium.

The participation of women and girls in football has risen by 2.3m since the Women's European Championship was held in England in 2022.

However, women remain significantly underrepresented in leadership positions.

Only a quarter of chief executive, chair or performance director roles in major UK sports are held by women and only 12% of sports federations are led by a female.

Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, remarked: "This is a proud day for Welsh football.

"We've put forward Wrexham and Cardiff as host cities, and it's exciting to think what a World Cup could bring to both cities and the communities around them.

Industry observers note that "In Llunio Cymru - our 10-year strategy - we've set ourselves the ambition of reaching the knockout stages in 2035. Some of the players who could take us there are learning the game at clubs across Wales today. Our job is to make sure that wherever a girl grows up in Wales, she can find a team close to home, have a coach who helps her develop and see a route to the Cymru shirt.".

Irish Football Association chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country".

"Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that," he added.

Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell remarked hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".

He added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come.".

Industry observers note that fifa's evaluation, published earlier this month, rated the bid 4.3 out of five. Its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".

That is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.

The bid evaluation remarked: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.

"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding complications.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, this blog is now closed.
  • Bosses at soccer team Bayern Munich have publicly questioned whether young Germany international Jamal Musiala's contract is valid in view of a debilitating neurological condition.
  • The remarks have been criticized by media and from several other quarters, among them the global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the officials of neglecting their "duty of care" toward their players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this blog is now closed. Read below for a roundup of headlines from and about Germany on the weekend of Saturday, November 21, and Sunday, November 22, 2026:.

Bosses at soccer team Bayern Munich have publicly questioned whether young Germany international Jamal Musiala's contract is valid in view of a debilitating neurological condition.

The remarks have been criticized by media and from several other quarters, among them the global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the officials of neglecting their "duty of care" toward their players.

You can read details on what has been happening at the top football club in this DW article: Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments.

Friedrich Christian "Mick" Flick, an art collector, investor and multimillionaire who belonged to one of Germany's richest business dynasties, has died aged 82 in Rosenheim in the southern state of Bavaria, his family has mentioned.

The family said in a statement issued on Saturday that Flick left behind "the memory of a life shaped by significant acts of generosity as a donor and patron, particularly in contemporary art and in promoting tolerance.".

Flick was the grandson of Friedrich Flick, who made a huge fortune in the Nazi era with his coal and steel business, partly by using forced labor.

This past came back to haunt the grandson in 2003 when he pledged to loan his world-famous collection of modern art to Berlin, with the Central Council of Jews in Germany calling the Flick Collection a "Göring Collection" and saying the loan was intended to wash clean the "blood money" from the Nazi era.

The collection, which contains some 2,500 works by 150 artists, was exhibited in parts in the German capital from 2004 to 2021.

Flick later mentioned in an interview that the widespread outrage, while hurtful, had forced him to look more closely at his family's history.

According to his family, Flick once said: "I have no guilt for my forefathers' conduct, but I feel a responsibility, a very special responsibility. Every German bears this responsibility. As a Flick, I bear it twice.".

Among other things, he collaborated with the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, which oversees Berlin's museums, to research his family's Nazi past.

He also set up a foundation in Potsdam, near Berlin, that aimed to combat xenophobia and racism and contributed €5 million ($5.4 million) to the foundation to compensate former forced laborers.

The family was also involved in a highly publicized party donations scandal in the 1980s that became known as the "Flick Affair.".

According to recent reports, "Mick" Flick married Countess Maya von Schönburg (1958-2019), the older sister of well-known socialite, businesswoman, art collector and artist Gloria von Thurn und Taxis, in 1985. The couple had three children.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is setting off on a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya.

Steinmeier will be accompanied by a business delegation and is expected to focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers during the trip.

On Monday, Steinmeier is to be received by Ivorian President Allassane Outtara in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's largest city and seat of government.

The next day, in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which, according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

On Wednesday, he will be received by Kenyan President William Ruto in Nairobi.

In Kenya, Steinmeier will also visit the Crescent Island Game Sanctuary on Thursday, the last day of his trip.

The Federal Institute for Hydrology (BfG) has mentioned it expects water levels in large rivers in western Germany, including the Rhine, to return to average or above in the next few days amid sustained rainfall.

It mentioned the water level at the key gauge in Kaub near Koblenz, located at an important bottleneck on the Middle Rhine, could reach some 3.3 meters (10.8 feet), more than 3 meters higher than the last recorded low-water readings.

The BfG stated it also expected rising water levels in the Weser and Danube rivers, with smaller increases in the Elbe and Oder.

The rising water level in the Rhine, an important shipping route, means that conditions for water-borne cargo transport have improved, according to Germany's inland navigation association BDB.

"The more abundant rainfall in the past days has caused the water level in the Rhine to rise considerably, and they will keep rising a great deal in the next few days as well, meaning that each ship has much more transport capacity again," stated Fabian Spiess, the deputy manager at BDB.

In the middle of the year, many ships were forced to drastically reduce the loads they carried, leading to economic losses that will not be recuperated any time soon, according to Spiess.

He cited the year 2018, in which shipping on the Rhine was also hindered by extremely low water levels, saying that the months of improved conditions at the end of that year had not been enough to make good the economic damage incurred.

The conservation NGO also noted that the current rain provided temporary relief to the environment but could not compensate for the negative consequences of the long dry period.

It said species of animals, such as amphibians and water insects, that lived in small bodies of water and moist habitats had been particularly impacted.

Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig claims that she intends to tighten the law on murders committed with "gender-specific" motives, with a particular focus on femicides perpetrated by men who are unable to accept a separation or the desire of a woman to live a self-determined life.

"A man kills, or attempts to kill, his partner or ex-partner almost every day in Germany," Hubig told the Sunday edition of the mass-circulation Bild newspaper.

"Any man killing a woman because she wants to leave him must be punished as a murderer," she mentioned, noting that in some cases, courts cite a man's deep sadness or fear of losing a partner to someone else as extenuating circumstances. This can lead to a lesser conviction of manslaughter.

She said that in future, courts should look more closely at such motives to determine whether they were based on sentiments of patriarchal possessiveness.

However, Hubig, who belongs to the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), remarked she was opposed to making femicide a separate category of crime, as some women's rights organizations have demanded.

She said that, in her opinion, doing so would have "no advantages over what we are intending — and much bigger disadvantages.".

The proposals are at the moment being debated within the coalition government and are expected to be presented to the states and associations for consideration before the end of the year.

They will then have to go before the Cabinet before being put before the parliament.

The powerful IG Metall union stated on Sunday it would call another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues.

Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding firm Meyer Werft and wind ​energy company Siemens Gamesa.

The union mentioned that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.

It says that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% ‌wage increase.

So far, employers have ⁠offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.

The DW newsroom says "Willkommen!" once more to all its readers as we resume our reporting on all things German.

Some good news is on the agenda: The Rhine River, which we can see from the window of our Bonn office, has recovered after a long period with little rainfall, meaning that the barges plying the waterway can load up properly again.

In other stories, the German president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, is setting off on a trip to Africa, during which he is set to visit three countries with a businesss delegation in tow.

And Germany's powerful IG Metall union has said it is launching another 24-hour strike on Monday amid an escalating pay dispute.

Read on to find out more about what is happening in Germany on Sunday, November 22.

In a recent development, we're pausing our Germany news blog for now. Come back for more on Sunday!

A new goal celebration was devised by Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha after his previous one caused controversy due to its religious aspect.

According to recent reports, after scoring the goal that secured Dortmund's 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach (see entry below), Nmecha knelt on one knee and crossed his arms in front of his chest. He then spread his arms, appearing to pray with his eyes closed.

Nmecha told broadcaster Sky that he intends to continue expressing his faith during goal celebrations, adding that he had once again given glory to Jesus.

However, he did not perform the controversial part of his usual goal celebration. In it, he removes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling.

This celebration has been heavily criticized, even by Dortmund's fan department.

Nmecha explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength.".

The gesture is used by Ballers in God, a network of Christian football players that has been criticized for the homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members.

Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke noted he asked the player not to do the celebration again.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha led his team to the top of the German Bundesliga table with a 1-0 victory over last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach.

Meanwhile, Bayern Munich was held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, and striker Harry Kane suffered a serious ankle injury. The Ballon d'Or winner is set to miss several months after undergoing ankle surgery earlier on Saturday.

Now, Dortmund has 24 points after 10 games, putting them two points ahead of Bayern and third-place Freiburg, who defeated Elversberg 1-0.

According to recent reports, fourth-place RB Leipzig had five different players score in a 5-1 victory over Union Berlin, bringing them to 21 points. Bayer Leverkusen scored four unanswered goals against Paderborn to stay in fifth place.

Germany is seeking to redress years of underinvestment by pouring billions into the modernization of public infrastructure and digital networks, and the transition to renewable energy sources.

But will the plan bring real change amid the labor shortages, burdensome bureaucracy and low productivity at the moment besetting Europe's largest economy?

DW takes a look at what is one of Germany's biggest public investment drives in decades in this video:.

Bundesliga powerhouse Bayern Munich concluded the 2025-26 financial year with record figures.

According to the financial report released Saturday at the club's annual general meeting, the club's total turnover was €988.2 million ($1.08 billion) — that is around €10 million more than the previous year.

In a recent development, operating profit (EBITDA) increased from €187.8 million to €190.8 million. Pre-tax profit was €35.3 million, and net profit for the year was €22.8 million.

Bayern had a particularly strong year in terms of sponsorships. Turnover increased by nearly €30 million, reaching €268.4 million. The club also set a record in merchandise sales, earning €152.8 million.

"We have achieved another record year," CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen said. "This shows that our club has a strong foundation. And we continue to invest to ensure the best possible conditions for the sporting success of our teams.".

Moreover, Bayern achieved another milestone. They reached 500,000 members — more than any other club in the world.

Over the past 12 years, the German giants have doubled their membership, growing from 250,000 in 2014 to 500,000 this year.

"Record champions, record members, record member champions," president Herbert Hainer stated.

Members hold a 70% stake in the club, which is well above the simple majority required by German rules.

The remaining 30% is owned by four German companies with roots in Bavaria: Adidas, Audi, Allianz, and Viessmann.

Sources indicate that bayern won the league and cup double in the 2025-26 season, losing only three of 53 games across all competitions. In Europe, the club made it to the Champions League semifinals.

Two and a half weeks after his sudden death, Free Voters leader Hubert Aiwanger, who was Bavarian Minister of Economic Affairs and Deputy Minister-President, was laid to rest in his hometown of Inkofen in Lower Bavaria.

According to recent reports, A memorial service was held at the Parish Church of the Presentation of the Lord and broadcast on a screen outside. According to the organizers, around 2,000 people attended the solemn service.

Aiwanger's funeral was open to the public. His longtime partner, Tanja Schweiger, the Regensburg district administrator (Free Voters), stated that Aiwanger had been "a man of the people.".

For that reason, she said, everyone "who liked and appreciated him" was warmly welcome. The politician had already been honored with a state funeral in Munich a week earlier.

Recent findings suggest that aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel on November 4 after canceling an appointment for health reasons. The 55-year-old died of natural causes.

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich's star striker, has pledged to return to the field for the vital matches at the end of the current campaign after undergoing surgery for a torn ankle ligament.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season," he wrote on social media above a photo of himself on his hospital bed, also thanking fans for their messages of support.

Kane, 33, was injured around 20 minutes into Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Bayern issued a statement on Saturday saying that Kane had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle but was expected to be out for three to four months.

England captain Kane, who finished the 2025–26 season with over 70 goals for club and country, was awarded the Ballon d'Or for his efforts.

Hubert Aiwanger, the deputy premier and economy minister of the southern state of Bavaria, is being buried on Saturday in his native town of Inkofen.

Aiwanger, the federal leader of the Free Voters (FW) party, died suddenly two weeks ago of natural causes at the age of 55 in a hotel in Berlin.

The funeral service ahead of the burial was open to the public, with police saying they expected some 1,000 participants.

A memorial service was held in Munich a week ago to honor Aiwanger.

Arsenal have 30 shots and still manage to mess it up

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5168 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.
  • There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came.
  • Industry observers note that the leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

Industry observers note that the leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It has been revealed that it was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-foot thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyokeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

So it proved on 75 minutes when Gyokeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside the post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

It has been revealed that it ended that way, with a heroic defensive performance from the Dortmund defence, including one memorable moment when substitute Serhou Guirassy’s determination to block a cross prompted a double ricochet off his own post. One could make the argument that there were times when it was “unbelievable”, as Arteta later stated, that the ball did not find its way in. Although there were also moments when the reasons were self-evident.

“There’s an element of luck,” the Arsenal manager said, “and there is an element of us finishing better.”.

Sources indicate that in fifth place in the league phase table, dropped points at home do not carry the same jeopardy in the group stage that they once did, yet even so there was a truth for Arteta to chew upon. This is a well-honed, major-game Arsenal Champions League side that he has built. One that reached the final last season and may well go close again, but as ever they seem to be doing so in spite of the great goalscorer that so many of their nearest rivals have at their disposal.

Arteta sounded that warning after defeat in the final in Budapest at the end of May and while changes have been made, it would be hard to argue that they have been fundamental. This was a good opponent – the leaders of the Bundesliga with many exports from English football who have been reconditioned for the German game. Those include Fábio Silva, Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham who had a second-half goal narrowly disallowed for offside.

Jobe Bellingham's goal RULED OUT for offside ❌ https://t.co/yaR8EX4Gs3.

After a chastening first half in which they found themselves in the teeth of the Arsenal press, Dortmund re-emerged as a much more effective attacking force. They found a way to break the Arsenal press by targeting Christos Tzolis and the run from the teenage French defender Joane Gadou that followed was exceptional. That created the goal for Beier, one of four shots on target from Dortmund – the same number as Arsenal.

Maximilian Beier punishes Arsenal to make it 1-1 😳 https://t.co/OOUmg9JnHo.

Dortmund, managed by the West German-born Croat Niko Kovac, did not always have Arsenal’s polish in possession but they certainly had the youth in their legs to match the English champions. In defence their captain Nico Schlotterback and Waldemar Anton will not have many better games. They might have been fortunate at times but they will also point to a penalty that was not given, when Gyokeres handled in his own area at the start of the second half.

According to recent reports, gyokeres’ first-half goal was certainly among the best he has scored for the club, invited to shoot by a Dortmund defence that simply stood off as he reached the edge of the area. He will not catch many as full as he did this one. More of a dig than a swish but with the useful consequence of packing a lot of power and a dip that meant goalkeeper Gregor Kobel saw it but could not pick out its flight.

Viktor Gyökeres what a HIT! 👏🔥 https://t.co/5m6FZoE8tQ.

Asked about the later Gyokeres miss, Arteta preferred to talk about other aspects of his striker’s performance. “The way he held up the ball, the way he threaded in behind and stretched the pitch,” Arteta said. “There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the Viktor that we needed.”.

Recent findings suggest that even so, there was some of the Gyokeres the Arsenal manager does not need as early as the end of the first half when he rolled out a wild shot over from Noni Madueke’s pass. Arteta was without David Raya who has a shoulder injury and there were no guarantees that he will be back for the Manchester City game on Sunday.

In a recent development, some good moments for young Bellingham against Myles Lewis-Skelly in the first half and then a goal disallowed after the break. That came after Beier’s equaliser when Dortmund were at their counter-attacking best. In the final stages, Arsenal pressed hard for the equaliser and although there were lots of shots it would be hard to say there were lots of chances. The one that got away was the one that fell to Gyokeres.

Sources indicate that arteta would later call it “a brilliant performance”. It was hard to shake the feeling from some of the caveats he added that, like everyone else, what he really thought – above all – was that his team should have won.

The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.

Recent findings suggest that that’s what we want [to finish in the top eight]. We have a big game against Manchester City at home on Sunday so we need to recover really well, we have four days to do that and sustain that momentum the way we are playing and the win will come.

According to recent reports, I think these are the best games. I’m really looking forward to it. Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same. We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We’re champions, we’re at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction.

Recent findings suggest that I feel like the performances from us up until the last shot was incredible at times. Definitely feels like two points dropped like the other day so, having dominated so much of the game we need to take all the points.

Sources indicate that I prefer this type of game [more open rather than against a deep defence], there are more breaks and opportunities to attack space. We it’s a low block it’s more about pass, pass, pass and wait for the right moment. I feel like we are well-suited to both types of game.

We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways. We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

The most important thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals when games are coming up.

But they are now four points off Real Madrid, who they play next, and more than likely PSG if they beat Roma tomorrow night.

Arsenal with a remarkable combination of poor finishing and bad decision-making in the final third. They ended the night with 56 touches in the Dortmund box and 29 shots, but only four of those shots were on target.

There was time for one late scramble, but at the final whistle it is the Borussia Dortmund fans celebrating the draw.

That result is going to make it very difficult for Arsenal to finish in the top two, but they will hope to have enough for a top-eight finish. They fail to win at home for the first time this season.

Dortmund had their moments, a very strong start to the second half when they could have scored more than once.

But over the piece, the story is Arsenal’s profligacy. Twenty nine shots on goal and more than two expected goals, but not enough to show for it.

Eze with a blocked shot but Arsenal do have Dortmund pushed back in their half for the final 90 seconds. Is there one more chance!

According to recent reports, kobel palms behind Rice’s delivery for another Arsenal corner. Feels like now or never if Arsenal are to find the winner.

Promising attack for Dortmund, but Timber blocked Karestas’s shot.

Then Arsenal go down the other end and win a corner through Hincapie’s persistence.

Just four minutes of added time.

Gabriel tries to win a header on the edge of Dortmund’s box but gives a foul away. Odegaard’s shot was blocked in the build up, he may have been better off crossing to the back post.

Arsenal with some good football through the lines involving Odegaard and Bruno Guimaraes, but then Konsa was the wrong man in the wrong place and committed a foul. Mikel Merino has replaced Viktor Gyokeres.

Some of the venom has gone out of the Arsenal backlash since the equaliser, but they continue to probe and push numbers forward.

It has been revealed that and Declan Rice hits the post! Brilliant slide-rule pass from Eze to release Rice into the box, and his first-time shot with his left foot cannons of the near post.

Sources indicate that dortmund have a throw deep in the Arsenal half now, after Kepa found himself in a tight spot and kicked to touch. Arsenal clear but Eze fails to bring them up the pitch.

Industry observers note that scramble in the Dortmund goal-mouth from an Arsenal free-kick, whipped in low by Odegaard right across the face of goal, kept alive by Hincapie at the back post and the ball bounced off the post when it looked like being an own goal. Kobel stays down to receive some treatment after colliding with the post.

It feels like Arsenal have restored some dominance since the changes, and after some messy play in the penalty box they have a corner. Punched clear by Kobel, before Madueke is fouled.

Arsenal crowd growing a little frustrated with Odegaard for turning down a shot at the edge of the box, and also failing to find Gyokeres with the pass.

Then Gyokeres misses a sitter! Brilliant ball from Odegaard, Gyokeres completely unmarked to meet to inswinging cross but he heads wide from six yards. Hincapie’s run maybe put him off but that would be generous.

Eze with a sloppy giveaway in his own half but Arsenal are not punished, before Rice sets the home team away with some great play in midfield. Eze feeds Gyokeres down the left, but not red player was in the six-yard box for a cross.

Then Madueke cuts inside from the right and shoots not far wide of the near post.

Arsenal’s inability to control this second half has made for a very entertaining game. Two teams going for it. Dortmund seem to accept they can’t defend their way to a result so they might as well try to attack.

Arsenal respond by throwing a couple of punches. First Eze’s shot was deflected over, before Anton made a magnificent block to deny Madueke. The game is swinging back and forth.

It has been revealed that jobe Bellingham wheels away in celebration thinking he has scored for Dortmund after Ryerson’s shot was saved from Kepa but the flag goes up for offside! It took Bellingham ages to realise, and his joy was cut short.

Replays show it was very, very tight indeed. The still image suggested Hincapie was playing him on, but VAR confirms offside as the decision.

Gyokeres with more gallant work in the channels for Arsenal but he is lacking some support at times, perhaps Eze and Guimaraes can change that.

Triple sub from Arsenal: Eze, Guimaraes and Timber replace Tzolis, Lewis-Skelly and White.

Industry observers note that the game is really good contest now, high level Champions League fare. Arsenal might need the win if they want a top-two finish.

Anton looks short of pace at the back for Dortmund, and Gyokeres streaks away from him down the left. Hincapie is the player found with the cut-back, and he tees up White for a shot that is always rising.

A flowing move but it ended at the feet of two defenders.

In a recent development, arsenal in search of an instant response, withe Odegaard finding Gyokeres with a pass into feet inside the box. His shot was blocked, and then Kobel saved Hincapie’s follow up header.

Madueke is then away from the right, shrugging off Anton, but no red shirt arrives in the six-yard box to reach his cross.

Arteta has been agitated since the half-time break and he will not have been impressed by the defensive work of Tzolis there. The Greek winger allowed Gadou to burst away and then dived in ineffectively as he ran downfield. These are the details and duels that Arteta obsesses over.

Goudou with a burst away from Tzolis and straight through the middle of the Arsenal midfield, and Beier’s first touch inside Gabriel was fantastic before he finished with a left-footed shot into the bottom corner. A very well-worked equaliser.

That’s how to break the Arsenal press. Run hard at Tzolis and give it everything. Great finish from Beier but an even better run from Joane Gadou to make it.

Maximilian Beier punishes Arsenal to make it 1-1 😳 https://t.co/OOUmg9JnHo.

Looking back at the penalty shout, Gyokeres’ arm was slightly away from his body.

Dortmund have a corner earned from a long throw, they are certainly growing into the contest now.

Cleared by Ben White at the near post, but there were loud Dortmund appeals for a handball penalty.

You never know with Uefa handball roulette, but VAR is of course checking.

Dortmund’s best move and opportunity of the game, Svensson with a low cross that beats Konsa and Beier was in front of Gabriel but he completely missed an attempted flick at the near post.

Then Madueke dances through a couple of challenges and bends a shot wide of the far post.

Recent findings suggest that kobel rushes outside of his box to clear a Gabriel pass aimed towards Tzolis. Gadou with a really poor pass across midfield when Dortmund were trying to keep position, wildly overhit which invited Arsenal to press and an aimless long ball followed.

According to recent reports, arsenal kick off the second 45 minutes. No changes from Arteta or Kovac.

A 70mph strike from Viktor Gyökeres against Dortmund 💨😮‍💨 https://t.co/hQHcCWvjUz.

Noni Madueke has started nine of Arsenal's last 11 matches in all competitions. This run of games has had such a positive effect on him. He looks more confident, relaxed and expressive than at any point in his #AFC career. Perhaps not having the pressure of Saka has helped him.

Dortmund’s gameplan clearly based on the build-up from goalkeeper to the two centre-halves and then forward. It is a different prospect doing it in the Bundesliga to doing it against the Arsenal pressing machine and over the course of the first half Dortmund have lost their nerve in that regards. Goalkeeper Gregor Kobel has gone long to the left flank more than he would have liked. But – and it’s a significant point – they have looked quite good once they have got into Arsenal’s half. The Gyokeres goal was a good dig that beat Kobel with the dip. It was close to him. For all that Gyokeres was invited to shoot. Not a yellow shirt near by.

Arsenal much the better team across the 45 minutes, racking up 14 shots and enjoying 61 per cent possession. A familiar tale though, is their failure to convert that dominance into a commanding lead. Borussia Dortmund gradually carried more threat as the half progressed, and Arsenal cannot count on the insurance policy of Raya in goal. They need the second goal.

A moment of sloppiness from Arsenal near the end of the half, and Kepa was almost caught out at his near post but managed to make the save at the expense of a corner. Nmecha won first contact, but his header looped over.

Industry observers note that madueke wins the ball back high for Arsenal and finds Odegaard, but the flag goes up for offside against Arsenal’s captain. Replays suggest it was close, but Gyokeres was pleased to see the flag after missing a good chance in the middle.

In a recent development, kepa patient on the ball for Arsenal to find Gabriel, who picks out Madueke with a diagonal over the top. Good close control from the winger, and he tees up Gyokeres for another attempt from just outside the box but he skies this one.

Dortmund win a corner from another Ryerson cross, he has looked their best outlet down the right. From the corner, Kepa was scrambling among bodies but Arsenal get away with it. Arteta wanted a foul on the goalkeeper.

Industry observers note that dortmund are a far more open opponent than Arsenal are used to facing in the Premier League, and they are fortunate not to have conceded more goals here, but they are willing to attack quite quickly in numbers. They’ve had five shots so far, and a couple of those were decent chances.

From the second phase of the next corner, Tzolis volleyed miles over when a shot was not on. Lewis-Skelly has been quietly effective in midfield for Arsenal, and there is applause for Ethan Nwaneri as he goes out to warm up for Dortmund. William Saliba is also out there stretching.

Incisive from Odegaard after Dortmund lost the ball in a dangerous position, and Rice charged straight through the middle, but was running out of steam as he took the shot and it deflected wide.

Corner taken short, well-worked between Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis, and the caught back falls for Gyokeres whose shot deflects wide for another corner.

In a recent development, no doubt Arsenal’s electric start of the opening 15 minutes has slowed, I’m not sure it would be possible or desirable to maintain that intensity across the 90 minutes. They are controlling the pace of and remaining patient, before Rice lets fly from almost 30 yards. Not far over the bar.

It has been revealed that dortmund with a nifty up, set and through but they had run offside. Gabriel then looks over the top for Hincapie, who was running over the top like a striker from left-back yet again.

Declan Rice with a crunching tackle in his own half that has the Emirates crowd on its feet, and Arsenal are flowing forward into space again but Gyokeres failed to pick the right final ball.

Recent findings suggest that now Dortmund have a corner after a Svensson shot deflects wide. Kepa claims with ease.

Hincapie, as we have seen with Arsenal’s full-backs all season, is popping up in advanced positions and he had a clear sight of goal but elected to pull the ball back when he should have put his laces through it. Well worked attack before then though, with Rice finding Odegaard between the lines and Gyokeres flicking the ball around the corner.

It has been revealed that better again from Dortmund, moving the ball with fluency from their own defensive third but Nmecha miscues his shot over the bar from the edge of the box. Kepa is then off his line to collect a chipped ball over the top.

Tzolis did well to harry and win the race to a long ball forward and he was close to flicking the ball into the path of Gyokeres.

Industry observers note that dortmund are starting to string some passes together, and they have a corner. This is one department where Arsenal will be appreciably worse without Raya but Hincapie heads clear.

Madueke then spins into space on the break and Gyokeres is free in the middle, but the winger slices the chipped pass.

Dortmund with their first attempt of the night after Ryerson swung in a cross from the left. Lewis-Skelly did well to compete in the air with Bellingham, before Silva kicked fresh air. Then with his second attempt, he volleyed over the bar.

Dortmund trying to settle into a spell of possession, but every pass feels like a chore for them at the moment and they are caught offside. Arsenal’s task now is to score the second while they have Dortmund where they want them. The German side will surely have a spell.

Gyokeres with another stretching run beyond Schlotterbeck, who is not the quickest. Arsenal completely dominant at the moment, but they do not always capitalise on these spells.

Chance for a second! Tzolis’ shot was parried by Kobel and Madueke’s rebound was blocked after he took a beat to control the ball. Could Madueke taken a swing first time?

In a recent development, arsenal are well worth that opening goal. Looking back at the replays of Gyokeres’s strike, it was an unusual technique, brushing the turf before the ball much as a golfer might do with a bunker shot.

It has been revealed that gyokeres may lack craft at times but there is no doubt he has power. That was a superb strike, dipping towards goal with real ferocity. Arsenal don’t score many goals from range but they have plenty of players who can do it. Gyokeres now has five goals and three assists in his last 10 games for club and country.

Madueke in acres of space down the right again, and there was too much space in front of the Dortmund back three for Gyokeres to receive the ball and turn. From there, Gyokeres decided to take the shot on and his laces technique produced power and dip which deceived the goalkeeper Kobel. It was not in the corner, but the loop did for him. Similar to one or two goals Morgan Rogers scored last season.

Viktor Gyökeres what a HIT! 👏🔥 https://t.co/5m6FZoE8tQ.

Dortmund find themselves beyond the halfway line for the first time in the game and there was an error from Rice that Fabio Silva failed to take advantage of. Arsenal soon back on the front foot though, and Odegaard’s shot from distance is blocked.

Industry observers note that noni Madueke has been Arsenal’s best attacker in recent weeks and he has started well here. He is really thriving in the absence of the injured Bukayo Saka. Perhaps that knowledge that he will start games has given him a sense of freedom that he was lacking before.

Arsenal have endured some slow starts to matches this season, but this has not been one of them. Dortmund cannot find room to breathe at the moment, and Arsenal are moving the ball with speed and authority. They are up the pitch again after Gyokeres wins a foul. Moments earlier, Madueke found Tzolis at the back post with a curling cross but Dortmund cleared his nod across goal.

Gyokeres with a scuffed shot from long range straight at the goalkeeper, but Arsenal continue to be on the front foot. Hincapie, their left-back challenged for the ball in the centre-forward position.

Very positive start from Arsenal, enjoying all of the ball in the first few minutes. Tzolis with a promising cross which was not far away from Hincapie, then Lewis-Skelly was in well to keep Dortmund pinned back. Madueke was found in space, and Tzolis connected with his ball to the back post, the volley bouncing over the ball.

Dortmund get the game under way, and line up almost all of their team on the left side of the pitch.

The entrance of players follows a pre-match light show and an airing of everyone’s favourite song The Angel, shunted back in the schedule to make room for the Champions League anthem.

Sources indicate that you can see Jobe is developing very well. As you also saw, he is now part of the England national team now.

Sources indicate that this is not by random, this is because he deserves it and he plays very well in the Bundesliga. Since he arrived, he’s developed day after day.

It has been revealed that in the beginning he needed a bit of time because the differences between the Championship and Bundesliga are huge, also the cultural aspect is different. He came to a fresh country, he had to learn now to live in Germany, but he’s there.

I’m very happy with him. He’s progressing and not only developing physically but with the ball and this is what we need.

I’m very impressed with them, with what Niko has done with the team, especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat that they are able to create.

We had them here in pre-season (a 3-2 defeat) and they demonstrated their quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that.

But we play at home in front of our crowd and we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

Mikel Arteta seems quite set on his left-back pecking order: Riccardo Calafiori starts on weekends, and Piero Hincapie starts in midweek. They are very different players (Calafiori is the more adventurous, while Hincapie is more of an old-school defender) and it seems that Arteta feels Hincapie is better suited to Champions League football. He’ll be tested tonight against the Bundesliga leaders.

It has been revealed that by Yannick HuberOn Tuesday, all eyes will be on Ethan Nwaneri. The Champions League clash between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund marks the 19-year-old’s return to the club where he grew up, where he became the Premier League’s youngest player and from whom he joined Dortmund on loan in the summer. It would be hard to imagine a more poignant setting. But for Nwaneri, facing Arsenal is about more than a reunion. It is also an opportunity to finally make his mark at Dortmund.

So far his time in Germany has not gone according to strategy. Nwaneri arrived with a considerable reputation and high expectations, but has become less prominent in recent weeks. His playing time has diminished and he has frequently had to settle for a place on the bench.

But there are several reasons to believe that, of all games, this meeting with his former club could give his Dortmund career fresh impetus.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; GyokeresSubs: Meslier, Porter, Saliba, Mosquera, Eze, Timber, Merino, Havertz, Calafiori, Guimaraes, Dowman.

Dortmund: Kobel, Ryerson, Anton, Schlotterbeck, Gadou, Svensson, Veerman, Nmecha, Bellingham, Beier, SilvaSubs: Drewes, Meyer, Bensebaini, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Nwaneri, Karetsas, Sabitzer, Mane, Albert, Dos Santos, Reggiani.

Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player the last time they played Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, and tonight he will have to make do without first-choice goalkeeper David Raya.

Arsenal’s manager struck an upbeat note when describing the shoulder or upper arm injury Raya sustained at Newcastle, and it appears he has avoided a long-term absence.

Even two weeks out, however, would mean Raya missing Premier League fixtures against Manchester City, Brentford and Spurs – possibly Arsenal’s most testing week of the season. Arteta did not rule out a return to face City on Sunday.

Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise against Dortmund, who are top of the Bundesliga and have won three of their four Champions League league phase games. They won at the Emirates in a pre-season friendly, and Jobe Bellingham and on-loan Arsenal attacker Ethan Nwaneri are among their ranks.

These Champions League fixtures can feel secondary in importance to Premier League fare because of the competition’s newly introduced format, but a top-two finish in the league phase is a serious incentive.

As Arsenal discovered to their benefit last season when they “won” the league phase, the top two teams are rewarded with home second legs all the way to the final.

Arsenal are currently third on 10 points and face Real Madrid at the Emirates next, the team above them in second, so victory this evening is essential to set up that occasion.

Arteta has tended to make between four and six changes for these games, and Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres are players pushing for starts after starting on the bench at Newcastle.

Also among the substitutes at St James’ Park was William Saliba, who is stepping up his return from a long-term back injury and could play his first minutes of the season tonight.

Chelsea are preparing for life after Xabi Alonso, following a 4-1 thumping at home to Leeds United.

That's according to one report, which states that despite hiring the Basque boss over the summer and backing him heavily with massive signings, such as Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers, the Blues are looking at the next man to take charge.

With Chelsea having lost three of the last five, a title challenge has turned into a battle for Europe, with the manager now under threat.

After a strong start to the season, Chelsea have tapered off, with Alonso facing several of the same problems that predecessors Liam Rosenior and Enzo Fernandez encountered during their Stamford Bridge stints.

Despite being given the title of 'manager' rather than 'head coach' – and thus wielding a little more power in recruitment – the club are still hampered by injuries, with the defence looking shakier than ever.

TEAMtalk have reported that despite Alonso's four-year deal, former Blues midfielder Cesc Fabregas is “right at the top of the list” to replace his former international colleague in the hot seat.

Como boss Fabregas won two league titles in West London and has masterminded an incredibly impressive surge towards the top in Italian football, with a recent Champions League thumping over Manchester United shocking Europe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Isiah Noel-Williams has been remanded in custody.

League Two footballer Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged with rape.

Noel-Williams, who plays for League Two side Barnet, has been charged with three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault by penetration, Hertfordshire Police stated.

The 23-year-old, of High Oaks, St Albans, was remanded in custody following a hearing at Hatfield Magistrates' Court on Saturday.

In a statement, the club mentioned it was "co-operating fully with authorities" and would determine further action "in due course".

Noel-Williams has also been charged with one count of engaging in sexual communication with a child, and one count of supplying a controlled (Class B) drug, police added.

In a statement, the London club mentioned: "Barnet FC can confirm that first-team player Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged and remanded in custody as part of a police investigation by Hertfordshire Constabulary.

"The club is co-operating fully with the authorities and will determine any further action in due course.

"As this is now a matter for the courts, the club will not be making any further comment.".

Noel-Williams, who previously played for Hemel Hempstead Town, Kettering Town, Matlock Town, Harrow Borough and Cheshunt, joined Barnet in June.
